name: Acmer K1 12W
tagline: The most powerful K1: an enclosed 2.4 kg mini diode that can also cut thin plywood
tldr: The K1 12W is the top version of Acmer's enclosed mini engraver: a 150 × 150 mm area in a 2.4 kg box with lid and tilt sensors and an exhaust fan, for $269.99. Acmer's chart gives up to 12 mm of plywood, without stating the number of passes; expect several passes beyond a few millimeters. Small area, USB-only connection and no camera are the trade-offs for the price.
mainObjective: Enclosed small-item engraving with real cutting of thin wood, on a tight budget

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

cut: Plywood up to 12 mm and paulownia up to 15 mm (Acmer chart, passes not stated)

pros: The only K1 that cuts 3 mm basswood in a few minutes, about 5–9 min for a 10 × 10 cm square in our benchmark profile
Enclosed box with lid and tilt sensors for $269.99
Fastest K1 engraving on wood, while keeping the same 0.08 × 0.08 mm spot
cons: Engraving speed capped at 10,000 mm/min, slower than enclosed rivals near the price
More smoke when cutting: the hose must be vented outside
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 12W version of the Acmer K1. Compare it with the 7W: pick the 12W if you plan to cut plywood shapes, ornaments or tags; box, area and software are identical. For $40 more than the 7W you mostly gain cutting speed.
proTips: Cut at low speed with several passes rather than at full speed, and keep the lid closed so the fan can clear smoke from the beam path. Check focus before each job, and test hardwood on scrap: it cuts far slower than the paulownia figures suggest.

faq.question: How thick can the K1 12W cut?
faq.answer: Acmer's chart gives 12 mm of plywood, 8 mm of black acrylic and 15 mm of paulownia, without stating speed or passes. Treat 3 mm as comfortable: our benchmark profile cuts a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood in about 5–9 min. Thicker stock needs several slow passes.

faq.question: K1 12W or Creality Falcon A1C 10W?
faq.answer: The Falcon A1C 10W ($369 on Creality's store, October 2026) adds a motorized lifting bed, auto-focus and Wi-Fi on the same 150 × 150 mm area. The K1 12W costs $269.99, is lighter and more compact, but connects by USB only. Pick the K1 to save $100, the A1C for taller objects and wireless use.

faq.question: Is the K1 12W worth $40 more than the 7W?
faq.answer: If you will cut wood, yes: the 12W roughly halves cutting time on 3 mm basswood in our benchmark profile. For engraving alone, the 7W at $229.99 is enough (Acmer store, October 2026).

editorialDepth.advantages: The 12W is the K1 to buy if you want an enclosed box at a very low price and still expect to cut ornaments, tags or small plywood shapes. Same 2.4 kg box, area and software as the other versions, with the most power for cutting and faster engraving on wood.
editorialDepth.limitations: The 150 × 150 mm area limits it to small objects, the speed cap of 10,000 mm/min slows large fills, and there is no camera, Wi-Fi or auto-focus. Acmer's cutting figures do not state the number of passes, and no in-depth independent review was available in October 2026.

standoutFeatures.title: Cutting in an enclosed box under $300
standoutFeatures.body: The 12W diode cuts 3 mm basswood in a few minutes in our benchmark profile, in a closed box sold $269.99.

standoutFeatures.title: 2.4 kg and fits on a shelf
standoutFeatures.body: At 286 × 273 × 190 mm, the K1 stores in a cupboard and moves easily between rooms or to a market stall.
